title: ～にしても — even if ～ / even granting ～
summary: Accepts a condition or situation for the sake of argument, and then says that even so, the following still holds: “even if ～, (still ～).” The latter half often gives advice, a request or a criticism.

patterns.form: 動詞・形容詞 普通形＋にしても
patterns.gloss: plain form + にしても (行くにしても、忙しいにしても)
noun + にしても (冗談にしても)

body.p: Verbs and i-adjectives take the plain form; nouns take にしても without だ (na-adjectives use the stem). It accepts the first point for now, then moves on to a “but still” statement. It means the same as にしろ and にせよ, with にしても being closer to speech.

As in 忙しいにしても、食事はきちんと取るべきだ, it shows you understand the circumstances but still hold the following view. The latter half is often the speaker’s opinion or judgment, rather than a sentence excusing the person because of the circumstance.

examples.ja: 行（い）くにしても、まず連絡（れんらく）してください。
examples.romaji: Iku ni shite mo, mazu renraku shite kudasai.
examples.tr: Even if you go, please contact me first.

examples.ja: 忙（いそが）しいにしても、食事（しょくじ）はきちんと取（と）るべきだ。
examples.romaji: Isogashii ni shite mo, shokuji wa kichinto toru beki da.
examples.tr: Even if you're busy, you should eat properly.
examples.note: Adjective plain form + にしても, then advice.

examples.ja: 冗談（じょうだん）にしても、そんな言（い）い方（かた）はよくない。
examples.romaji: Jōdan ni shite mo, sonna iikata wa yokunai.
examples.tr: Even as a joke, that way of putting it isn't good.
examples.note: Noun + にしても (no だ), then criticism.

pitfalls: Do not add だ to nouns or na-adjectives: × 冗談だにしても, ○ 冗談にしても.
It is different from にしては (“for a ～”). Do not confuse them.
